Subject: Clarify: p50/p95 measurement methodology and carve-outs for Hosted API SLA

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We liked the latency profiles, but legal and SRE need precise language for the Hosted API SLOs before we can move forward. A few concrete asks so we can draft the addendum: 

- Confirm how Redwood computes p50 and p95 for the Hosted API: is it per-request aggregation, bucketing, or a different two-stage approach?
- What measurement window do you recommend for a production SLA (Finix prefers something that matches our hourly billing cadence but legal thinks 24h makes more sense).
- Do you provide a sample evidence package (raw buckets / dashboard) for a representative week? Ops asked for a CSV or script they can run against the sample dataset.
- We need a clear list of carve-outs: scheduled maintenance, provider region failover, major incidents, DDOS (if detected). Please indicate thresholds (e.g., maintenance >5m?).

Target SLOs we proposed internally: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 320ms (applied to production traffic). Are those achievable with your hosted configuration in us-east-1? If not, please propose an alternate target and explain measurement differences.

Can you send sample SLA wording we can hand to legal plus a short technical note for SRE?

Best,

Subject: Re: Clarify: p50/p95 measurement methodology and carve-outs for Hosted API SLA

Hi Signe — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front: yes, we can meet close to the targets in us-east-1 for typical text-generation workloads, and we can provide a one-week evidence package and a runnable sample script. Below is our recommended measurement approach and suggested carve-outs. I attached a small sample script (slo_sample_script.py) and a dashboard snapshot.

1) Measurement method (recommended): two-stage bucketed quantile aggregation
   - Stage A (instrumentation): we record per-request tail-to-tail server-side latency for every request (accept -> last token emitted). Each request is one data point.
   - Stage B (bucketization & aggregation): we compute per-1-minute buckets of latency and calculate the per-minute p50 and p95. To produce the contractual SLO for a day, we take the distribution of those per-minute quantiles over the 24-hour window and compute the target quantiles across the minute-level values, weighting each minute by the number of requests observed in that minute. Practically: we produce a vector of per-minute p95s with associated counts and then compute the weighted p95. This reduces sensitivity to extreme single-request outliers while preserving minute-level variability.

Why this approach? It balances noise control (very short bursts) and fairness across traffic-volume variations (so low-traffic minutes don't dominate). It also maps cleanly to bucketed monitoring (the dashboard shows per-minute bands).

2) Measurement window recommendation: 24-hour rolling window for contractual enforcement, evaluated daily. For operational alerts we recommend 5-minute and 1-hour windows. For billing or SLA dispute evidence we provide the 24h rolling result and the underlying per-minute vector for the period in question.

3) Carve-outs (suggested language):
   - Scheduled maintenance: automated carve-out when maintenance is declared > 5 minutes in a single 1-hour window; customer and Redwood must have recorded maintenance at least 48 hours in advance for planned maintenance to be excluded.
   - Cross-region provider failover: carve-out if underlying cloud provider signals region-level outage impacting >=20% of capacity for >10 minutes.
   - Major incidents & security events: carve-out when Redwood declares a Sev1 incident or a verified third-party DDoS mitigation event; incidents must be documented in the incident report.
   - Network partitioning between customer VPC and Redwood (for Private/Dedicated customers) — negotiated per-deployment.

4) Evidence & audit artifacts: we provide: per-minute CSV of latencies, aggregated per-minute p50/p95, request counts, and the dashboard snapshot. We can also produce a signed summary report for the billing window.

5) Achievability in us-east-1: for typical 8–12 token responses at our default model catalog entry (optimized open model), p50 ~ 80–110ms and p95 ~ 200–280ms under steady load. If Finix traffic includes long responses (>32 tokens) or large prompt sizes, p95 will move up — we can propose a model/quantization profile or a dedicated pool for strict guarantees.

Next steps: I’ll draft suggested SLA text and send it to legal and SRE. Lauren, can you help with the formal SLA wording? Kim, can you attach the sample dashboard link and confirm whether we can provide the signed summary report (we usually do).

Marcus Lin

Hi Signe — legal here. Thanks Marcus for the clear technical framing; that two-stage approach looks reasonable. A couple of items we'll need in the SLA addendum so our counsel signs off: 

- Exact wording for \"measurement unit\" (we propose: \"p50 and p95 measured on server-side request latency, computed from 1-minute bucketed quantiles and aggregated via weighted quantile over a 24-hour rolling window\").
- A non-exhaustive carve-out list with thresholds (we will use the thresholds Marcus suggested as a starting point).
- Service credits formula: what is Redwood comfortable offering for missing a single-day SLO? (Finix has asked for a transparent credit schedule tied to the percentage of minutes that exceed the p95 target).
- Evidence retention: we need the per-minute CSVs stored for at least 90 days for audit — confirm retention.

Kimberly — can you draft the SLA paragraph and a short appendix listing evidence artifacts (CSV layout, retained fields)? I'll loop in Legal after that. Signe, happy to run a one-week measurement trial with the proposed settings and provide the csv+dashboard. If the trial looks good, we can bake the sample text into the SA.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is perfect. Ops confirms the proposed trial approach. A few action items from us: 

- Please start a one-week trial in our staging org and share the per-minute CSV export and the dashboard link (that dashboard link in "related_links" is ideal).
- We accept the 24-hour rolling window for contractual measurement. For the service credits, Finix prefers a simple schedule (e.g., miss p95 on a full day -> 5% credit of monthly invoice; two days -> 10%). We can negotiate exact numbers during the addendum draft.
- Carve-outs look reasonable; please include the exact maintenance notice and outage thresholds in the draft.

We'll hand this to Legal after your SLA paragraph and appendix. Looking forward to the sample artifacts.

Best,
Signe
